# <span id="aanchor301"></span> Exception Resolver

<a href="#" class="selected">Overview</a> \| [Exception Grid](Exception%20Resolver_Grid.md) \| [Object Explorer](Exception%20Resolver_Object%20Explorer.md) \| [Notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md) \| [Settings](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md)

## Overview

Accessing this screen requires **Data Exceptions - Can View** permissions.

Exceptions flag suspect data that has been imported or manually added to a meter, location, source, or ticket. Running validations for a meter after data has been added can also create exceptions. A complete list of FLOWCAL exceptions is available in the [Exception Description Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Exception%20Description%20Editor.md).

FLOWCAL typically generates exceptions when it detects:

- Differences between an imported characteristic and a master characteristic.
- Imported (original) or edited data that lies outside established set points.
- Missing data that it needs for performing a calculation.
- Missing data where it expected data.

The Exception Resolver lists all exceptions for a selected object, allowing you to investigate causes and determine how to resolve the issues.

FLOWCAL cannot retrieve more than 500,000 exceptions from the database at a time. It retrieves meter exceptions first, followed by location and source exceptions.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 1013;height: 449;" />

<div class="procedure">

To access the Exception Resolver:

- Click the **Exception** tile on the main screen;
- Go to **Review** \> **Exception Resolver**; or
- Click **More** on an [Exception Resolver widget](../../Dashboard%20Manager/Dashboard%20Manager_Exception%20Resolver.md) on the main screen (if configured).

If you access the Exception Resolver from an Exception Resolver widget, the data grid displays the exceptions for the selected list and follows the user preferences for filters.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Filter Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Filter Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Filter Options">

The following filter options are available in the Exception Resolver:

- **System** - Contains the FLOWCAL systems where you are a member.

- **Object Type** - Determines the type of data that displays in the exception grid. This selection determines the items that will be available in the Object Search box. Available object types are:
  - **Meter** - Displays exceptions for specific meters.
  - **Location** - Displays exceptions for a location, including exceptions for all associated meters, locations, and tickets in the location hierarchy. You can further filter location objects by location type (balance, liquid cavern, comparison, inventory, segment, station, and tank).
  - **List** (default) - Displays exceptions for meter/location lists. Location lists display location exceptions, including exceptions for immediate associated meters, locations, and tickets. FLOWCAL does not display exceptions for members that are not immediate members.
  - **Close Group** - Displays exceptions for associated meters. FLOWCAL does not display exceptions for locations in close groups.
  - **Source** - Displays exceptions for sources.
  - **Source List** - Displays exceptions for source lists.
  - **Ticket** - Displays exceptions for standalone tickets (tickets not associated with a location). Object Search is not available.
  - **Sample** - Displays exceptions for standalone samples (samples not associated to an LQ source). Object Search is not available.

- **Object Search** - Select an object for which to view exceptions. The list contains the 10 most recently used objects of a given type, followed by the remaining list of objects you have access to based on security. For example, if you select Meter as the object type, the list contains the 10 most recently used meters, followed by the rest of the meters to which you have access.

  You can expand the Object Search drop-down list by clicking and dragging the bottom-right corner. You can also manually search for items within this list.

- **Show Quality Source Object Selector** - Includes exceptions for an associated quality source. This link is only available after you select an object.

- **Date Selector** - Select a datetime range for exceptions you want to display, if necessary. Three date options are available:

  - **None** - Displays exceptions for all of time.
  - **Effective Date** - Displays exceptions based on the effective date of the associated data.
  - **Generated Date** - Displays exceptions that were generated on a specific date.

  By default, the Date Selector is set to Effective Date with the First Date being the beginning of the previous month at 00 hour (for example, if the current date is April 10, then the First Date is March 1) and the Last Date being the current date and the start of the next hour from the system time.

  The First and Last Date/Hour are inclusive.

  Select the start time for the First Date by clicking in the field to access the calendar, and then clicking the **Start of Time** button or pressing **Alt+S**.

  Select the end time for the Last Date by clicking in the field to access the calendar, and then clicking the **End of Time** button or pressing **Alt+E**.

  If the **First Date** value is later than the **Last Date** value, the Date Selector displays in red, indicating that there is an issue with the dates.

- **Legend/Status Filter** - Click the checkboxes next to each status type to filter the exceptions by status (Acknowledged, Resolved by Late Data, Resolved by User, Pending, Unresolved).

  FLOWCAL retains status filter changes that you make from the Exception Resolver screen until you close FLOWCAL, even if you exit the Exception Resolver. To save status filter selections across sessions, go to **Settings** \> **User Preferences**.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Toolbar Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Toolbar Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Toolbar Options">

The following options are available on the Exception Resolver toolbar:

- 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> **Reset** - Clears the grid and restores the settings to the user preferences that are defined in **Settings Manager** \> **User Preferences**.

- 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 15;height: 9;" /> **Email** - Opens the email dialog box and populates the email with the selected exceptions. This option is also available when you right-click an exception in the grid.

- 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 17;height: 22;" /> **Export to Excel** - Exports all data from the Exception Resolver (excluding summary rows).

  The Excel export might include exceptions that are not currently visible in the grid due to column filtering. Exceptions filtered out through parameters at the top of the form are not included in the export.

- 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 18;height: 17;" />**Add Note** - Adds a note to objects for the selected exception. This option is also available when you right-click on an exception in the grid. (See: [Notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md))

- 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 18;height: 17;" /> **Settings** - Opens the Settings screen so that you can specify user preferences. (See: [Exception Resolver Settings](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md))

A **Refresh** button is also available beneath the Status Filter checkboxes. Click this button to refresh the grid based on the filters/settings that you defined. The total number of exceptions displays in the bottom right corner of the screen, labeled **Count=**. If you change any settings after FLOWCAL populates the data grid, the data grid clears and you will need to click the **Refresh** button again.

</div>

<span id="Function"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Function Buttons">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Function Buttons</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Function Buttons">

The following function buttons are available to change the status of exceptions:

- **Acknowledge** - Update the status of selected exceptions to "Acknowledged". This button is only enabled when you select one or more unresolved or pending exceptions.

Use this status for exceptions that have been reviewed and deemed acceptable.

- **Pending** - Update the status of selected exceptions to Pending. This button is only enabled when you select one or more unresolved exceptions.

Use this status for exceptions that require resolution at a later time.

- **Unresolve** - Update the status of selected exceptions to "Unresolved". This button is only enabled when you select one or more acknowledged or pending exceptions.

Use this status for exceptions that have not been addressed and need attention.

- **Resolve** - Access the flagged data for selected exceptions so that you can investigate or resolve the issue. This button is enabled when you select any exception. Double-clicking an exception will also direct you to the flagged data.

  - Meter exceptions open the Volume Editor to the hour the exception occurred.
  - Location exceptions open the Location Close Approval screen for the appropriate record.
  - Source exceptions open the Source Analysis Editor for the appropriate record.
  - Ticket exceptions open the Ticket Detail Editor.
  - Sample exceptions open the Sample Analysis Editor.

  The Resolve button is only available if you have **Data Exceptions - Can Edit** privileges and the **Exception Resolver - Linkages** module. You cannot resolve event-generated exceptions, such as a purged all data exception; you can only acknowledge them. You can only update an exception status for an exception, not a summary (group) row.

- **Done** - Close the exception resolver.

To require an edit reason for exception status changes, enable the Require Edit Reason for Exceptions option in the [System Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20General%20Tab.md) screen.

</div>
